deviations.what: Buttons keep their meaning in the db: each discord.message button may carry a value object; the port gives it an opaque custom_id (the given custom_id as prefix plus a generated token) and stores the value in a discord_buttons collection before posting; the gateway attaches the stored value to the discord.button.clicked event as data.value. The custom_id no longer encodes repo, number and sha
deviations.reason: no existing piece can parse repo/number/sha out of a custom_id (no string builtin; refs and templates have no string functions); operator 2026-10-31: the button is published and its id saved, the meaning of the id kept in the db, so button and message text carry no parsing constraint (option B chosen over the run.read workaround)

deviations.what: The merge fence also pins where the button came from: discord_buttons records the run and workflow that posted each valued button, the discord.button.clicked event carries them (data.posted_by), and github.merge refuses unless that posting run's workflow is trusted in a new merge_prompt role (shipped empty, like merge). Going live pins two digests: the prompt workflow and the merge workflow
deviations.reason: code review of #129, finding 4: the fence checked the merge workflow and the click but not who posted the button whose stored value it merges, so an untrusted workflow could post a merge-prefixed button naming another PR; operator 2026-10-31 chose to pin the prompt too; builds on deviation d1 (stored button values)

deviations.what: Replace the merge and merge_prompt digest pins with a one-time button code: discord.message issues a code for a button with code: true, stored with its value; github.merge checks the click's code (exists, this button, unused, bound to repo/number/sha) and marks it used by compare-and-set before merging; the ROLE_MERGE and ROLE_MERGE_PROMPT pins and the prompt_not_trusted and workflow_not_trusted fences are removed
deviations.reason: Operator 2026-10-31: workflows are configuration, not code, so changing one (moving the prompt to #pull-requests) must not need a code PR. The operator chose to replace both pins with a code issued on the button and validated when the click is consumed; the trust becomes the operator's click (users filter) plus a valid unused code. Reverses d2.

deltas.behavior_text: A button's meaning lives in the store, not its custom_id: a valued button is posted as <custom_id>:<token>, its value is stored in discord_buttons before the post, and the click carries it as data.value
The merge fence is the operator's click plus a one-time button code bound to repo/number/sha and used up by compare-and-set, instead of pinned merge and merge_prompt workflow digests
The merge and merge_prompt trust roles and their refusals (workflow_not_trusted, prompt_not_trusted) are gone; moving the prompt's channel or text is a live edit, not a release
A merge that did not happen (GitHub refused it, the PR closed, a secret failed) hands the code back so a new click can merge; a store failure in the fence is a retryable store_unavailable
